first_impression.summary_in_own_words: A guide to getting married in Portugal, sorted by region, with the legal steps for our passports, run by a company that has a planning service called Wedded Concierge with one advisor per couple. It reads more like a very good destination guide than a full service destination wedding planner's page.

attention_map.quote: Get Married in Portugal, from a Sintra Palace to an Algarve Cliff
attention_map.why: Clear and pretty. The line 'plans weddings in Portugal for couples from Australia, the United States and the United Kingdom, with one Wedded Advisor from first enquiry to the wedding weekend' is exactly what I want to hear, if it actually lands in the hero and not buried down in s10. The brief says 'here or in s10', so I might not see it up top.

attention_map.quote: Fallback until sign-off: a non-numeric line naming Wedded Concierge and one Wedded Advisor, or hide the strip.
attention_map.why: This is the spot where I check proof before anything else. If it is hidden or just repeats the service name, there is nothing to look at. No press, no numbers, no names.

attention_map.quote: Fall for Portugal Before You Choose a Venue
attention_map.why: Pena, Douro, Ponta da Piedade. Nice, but I can get sightseeing from any travel site. The Monserrate scaffolding note to Q1 2027 is the part that made me trust it a little: someone is paying attention.

attention_map.quote: Setting; Best months; Nearest airport (code); Guests
attention_map.why: Same lines on every card is great for comparing. But 'Nearest airport (LIS)' with no drive time does not tell me if the venues are within two hours of an airport. The guest line being blank or 'Ask your Wedded Advisor' is a dodge for a 120-guest wedding.

attention_map.quote: Queluz and the National Palace of Sintra can be needed for state events, and events on those dates may have to be cancelled
attention_map.why: That is the kind of detail a senior planner tells you upfront. Genuinely useful and a bit alarming, in a good way.

attention_map.quote: visa-free short stays on Australian, US and UK passports
attention_map.why: Fine, expected. Nothing I would not already assume.

attention_map.quote: Exclusivity can mean paying for unoccupied rooms; a buy-out is often separate from the venue fee
attention_map.why: This is about how supplier costs are structured, which is one of my real questions. Helpful, even without numbers.
Separate US and UK routes, official sources, 'checked October 2026'. Better than most planner sites. I would bookmark this tab alone.

attention_map.quote: Fallback until then: explain what drives cost (guest count, region, season, nights at the venue, exclusivity) with no figures
attention_map.why: If the euro table does not get signed off, I get a list of things that affect cost and no numbers at all. That feels evasive when I am comparing firms that show ranges.

attention_map.quote: Venue nights with rooms, welcome dinner, ceremony, long dinner, late party, Sunday brunch, an on-the-day coordinator.
attention_map.why: This is the closest the page gets to 'end to end', but it describes what a weekend is, not what you actually do. 'An on-the-day coordinator' sounds smaller than full service.

attention_map.quote: Guest website in Wonderland Studio with the button 'Start for free'.
attention_map.why: A free DIY website tool sits oddly next to a full service promise. It makes the brand feel mass market.

attention_map.quote: hidden at launch: only 2 Portugal real weddings
attention_map.why: Can we see weddings you have done here? Apparently not. That is the one thing I look for before the form.
Proposals, birthdays, honeymoons. Not why I am here; it dilutes the wedding focus.

attention_map.quote: a Wedded Advisor explains fees in your currency on the first call
attention_map.why: Good that it is my currency, but I still do not know if it is a flat fee, a percentage or commission from venues. No advisor names or faces, founder quote removed. 'Wedded Privileges Tier 1' means nothing to me.

attention_map.quote: Can US or UK citizens marry legally in Portugal?
attention_map.why: Useful, but repeats the tabs. Nothing about the service itself.

attention_map.quote: Cristiano Ronaldo and Georgina Rodriguez's wedding
attention_map.why: Celebrity gossip links on a page where I am deciding who handles a six-figure wedding. Feels like a magazine, not a planner.

questions_answered.question: What exactly does end-to-end include?
questions_answered.evidence: s6 lists what a weekend 'can include' and 'one Wedded Advisor from first enquiry to the wedding weekend', but nowhere says what the firm actually does: venue sourcing, supplier contracts, design, guest travel, legal paperwork, on-the-day team.

questions_answered.question: Why an Australian company for a wedding in Europe?
questions_answered.evidence: Nothing addresses it. The brand line mentions couples from Australia, the US and the UK, which helps the framing, but there is no reason given to pick this firm over a planner based in Portugal.

questions_answered.question: How far is it from a major airport?
questions_answered.evidence: Each region card names the nearest airport (LIS, FAO, OPO, FNC), and Lisbon may say 'many Lisbon-area venues are 15 to 30 minutes from the centre'. No drive times for the Douro, Alentejo or Algarve venues.

questions_answered.question: How are fees and supplier costs structured, and in what currency?
questions_answered.evidence: The venue charges box explains buy-outs, per-day or per-guest fees and VAT checks; costs in EUR with a note that AUD, USD and GBP vary. But the firm's own fee is 'explained on the first call' and the euro table may not appear at all.

questions_answered.question: Can we see weddings you have done here?
questions_answered.evidence: Real weddings block is hidden at launch; the brief itself calls it a 'known gap'.

objections_triggered.objection: No proof they have done weddings in Portugal
objections_triggered.triggered_by: s8 hidden, B8 proof strip hidden or non-numeric, founder quote removed
'a Wedded Advisor explains fees in your currency on the first call'

objections_triggered.objection: Vague scope: not sure this is truly full service
objections_triggered.triggered_by: 'an on-the-day coordinator' and 'Start for free' guest website

objections_triggered.objection: Why would we use this firm rather than a local Portugal planner?
objections_triggered.triggered_by: No answer anywhere; 'Why book through Wedded Concierge rather than the venue directly' limited to approved facts only
Airport codes but no drive times on most region cards
Not triggered: costs are in EUR and fees promised in our currency

trust_signals_noticed: Legal steps by passport from official sources with 'checked October 2026'
Honest palace caveats: state-event cancellations and Monserrate scaffolding to Q1 2027
Venue charges box explaining buy-outs and unoccupied rooms
One named advisor model from enquiry to wedding weekend
Euro costs with a currency note rather than AUD only
turn_offs_noticed: Vague scope: no list of what the firm itself handles
No senior planner names or faces
No real weddings in Portugal shown
Free DIY guest website next to a full service pitch

emotional_response.overall: Impressed by the homework, unmoved by the people.
emotional_response.detail: I trust that they know the rules. I have no sense of who would be planning our wedding or whether they would care about it. 'Emotionally invested' does not come through at all; there is no human on the page.

payload.decision_reason: I would bookmark it for the legal-by-passport tab and the palace rules, which are better than what the other firms show. But I would not enquire: there are no weddings they have done in Portugal, no planner faces, and the fee is 'explained on the first call'. Scope, proof and fees are my bar, and only the region and legal parts clear it.
payload.verbatim_reaction: This is a really thorough guide, honestly more useful than some of the planner sites I have open. But I came looking for a full service destination wedding planner and I can't tell who these people are, what they actually handle, how they charge, or whether they have ever done a wedding in Portugal. 'Real weddings: hidden.' That is the tab I would have clicked first. I'll keep it for the legal stuff and go enquire with the firm that showed me a Sintra wedding they planned.
